about: Fictional educational profiles for the BCA project demo. Not real people, not registered donors, not patients. Kept separate from donors.json so they never appear in distance searches or donor counts.

profiles.name: Tanvi Joshi
profiles.demoStatus: DEMO ONLY — NOT A REAL DONOR
profiles.locationNote: Test location (city centre). Not a real address, not shown on the map and not used in distance searches.
profiles.note: O− red cells carry no A, B or RhD antigen, so in an emergency they can be given before the patient's group is known. This applies to RED CELLS only: O− plasma contains anti-A and anti-B, so it is not universal plasma. The blood bank still checks other antigens and antibodies (crossmatch).

profiles.note: An AB+ person has no anti-A or anti-B and is RhD positive, so in the ABO/Rh system they can receive red cells of any group. profiles.name: Prakash Patil
profiles.demoStatus: DEMO ONLY — NOT A REAL DONOR
profiles.locationNote: Test location (city centre). Not a real address, not shown on the map and not used in distance searches.
profiles.note: The Bombay phenotype (first described in Bombay, now Mumbai, in 1952) has no H antigen. Routine ABO tests show it as group O, but the person has anti-H as well as anti-A and anti-B, so they can receive blood ONLY from another Bombay-phenotype donor. It is NOT a universal group. Shown here as an educational example: a real diagnosis needs laboratory confirmation (e.g. testing with anti-H).
